title: Candidate 48 exact moduli are not the compact SO(4)/U(1) orbit

claim.statement: The five-parameter candidate-48 finite moduli cannot be identified locally with the five-dimensional compact SO(4) orbit of the canonical vacuum in the Spin(2,3) embedding.
claim.consequence: The v646 2+2 Hessian anisotropy is not repaired by interpreting the known finite moduli as Goldstone coordinates of Lorentz breaking.

setup.moduliTangents: four U(2) seed tangents in orbit (4,8), plus the eta tangent
setup.comparisonTangents: commutators of the six compact even SO(4) generators with the same vacuum

interpretation: Matching dimension five is accidental and insufficient: the principal-angle audit shows the tangent spaces are different.
At least four independent exact-modulus directions are orthogonal to the compact SO(4) orbit at the canonical vacuum.
The known flat family therefore contains non-Goldstone or accidental moduli relative to this SO(4).

A formal SO(4) Reynolds projection of the v646 eight-dimensional seed Hessian gives 0.2941723196552552 times the identity, but this average is not integration over the candidate's known moduli and is not a single-vacuum local Hessian.
falsifiers: A different, explicitly justified map from finite-moduli parameters to the same carrier vacuum could overturn the tangent comparison if its Jacobian spans the SO(4) commutator orbit.
A different compact SO(4) embedding inside SO(5) may have a different orbit; this result concerns the SO(4) selected by the established Spin(2,3) continuation.
Numerical equality would require all five principal cosines to approach one; the observed spectrum is far from that threshold.
nextBranches: Classify the five moduli tangents under the residual U(1) and compare them with the five compact-orbit tangents.
Test whether the accidental moduli become lifted by an SO(5)-completion counterterm.
Construct a two-order-parameter toy separating moduli-space averaging from compact-orbit averaging.

evidence.reportingNote: Projector distance evaluated from principal angles to avoid materializing a 67712-square projector.
